subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 1976, the film The Omen was released in theaters.
• According to the film's credits, the music was composed by Jerry Goldsmith.
• Jerry Goldsmith was widely known to be a professional film composer.
• A film composer creates original musical scores for movies.
• However, the main theme was actually written by a session musician named Carol Douglas.
prompt: The student wants to identify the real composer of The Omen's main theme. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Jerry Goldsmith, whom The Omen's credits indicated was the film's composer, was widely known to be a professional film composer.
choices.B: The credits of the film The Omen indicated that the music was composed by Jerry Goldsmith.
choices.C: The real composer of The Omen's main theme was Carol Douglas, though the film's credits listed Jerry Goldsmith as the composer.
choices.D: A session musician who was not credited in the film actually wrote the main theme of The Omen.

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer. The sentence identifies the main theme's real composer, explaining that Carol Douglas wrote it though Jerry Goldsmith received the official credit.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect. The sentence explains that Jerry Goldsmith was known as a professional composer; it doesn't identify the main theme's real composer.
